paragraphs: Here's what I love, friend. This man doesn't demand anything. He just drops to his knees and says, "If You are willing, You can make me clean." (Mark 1:40) He knows Jesus has the power, and he trusts himself to Jesus' heart. That's a bold way to pray, and it's an honest one.

Now look at the answer: "Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man." (Mark 1:41) Then come the words "I am willing," and then "Be clean!" (Mark 1:41) Under the Law, a leper had to live alone, outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46), so I think that touch meant a lot to a man who'd been kept at a distance. When you come to Jesus with the thing you can't fix, you can bring it honestly, just like this man did, and trust the heart of the One you're asking.

Then comes the part that makes me laugh and wince at the same time. Jesus gave a stern warning to tell no one, and the man "openly began to proclaim and spread the news." (Mark 1:43, 45) I get it, friend, I really do. But the passage still ends with people coming to Jesus "from every quarter." (Mark 1:45) Even when we don't get it all right, Jesus is still the One people come to.
